purpose: Reference extraction field meanings. Apply only to selected fields. Use only supplied IDs.
kind: Use claims when source facts or exact-token obligations exist. Meaningful prose requires claims; claims may be empty only when there are exact-token obligations but no prose facts to extract. Use no_feature_claim with a reason only when neither exists.
claims: One independently meaningful source fact per entry. Include meaningful identity and purpose headings. Separate independent behavior, implementation and verification facts.

category.business: Feature identity, purpose, goals or observable product behavior, including outputs, conditions and behavioral constraints. Preserve technical qualifiers with the behavior.
category.design: An explicit design decision or constraint.
category.technical: Source-stated implementation mechanisms, dependencies, runtime environments, interfaces or protocols. Technical terminology alone does not make observable behavior technical.
category.validation: An explicit obligation to test, inspect, measure or otherwise verify correctness. A behavioral requirement being testable does not make it a validation claim.
category.implementation_assumption: An assumption stated by the source, never an invented default.
category.open_question: A question left unresolved by the source.
category.scope_guard: An explicit inclusion, exclusion or scope boundary.

citations: IDs of the source_lines that state the complete claim, including its conditions. The cited lines become the claim's wording; lines from several top-level list items become one claim per item.
nodes: Write the complete reason as a string, or use {"fragments":[text or permitted references]} for explicit composition. Fragments concatenate exactly; strings include their own separators.
